Rational finite programs certify both sides uniformly over nonempty closed baseline intervals with supplied endpoint enclosures. An independent dense-baseline pilot selects a certified neighborhood game; explicit full-interval randomization restores unchanged finite-sample coverage. A growing public cutoff stitches these decisions to observable count procedures, retaining the matched global risk and length orders. The separate Gaussian endpoint concerns a scalar contrast on qualified local neighborhoods.
gap: Fixed-law transport scores and common-contrast efficiency projections do not characterize honest decision values when the informative arm counts remain finite. Generic confidence-region optimization does not justify replacing an estimated continuous baseline by an exactly observed baseline.
